title: Coalgebra reconstruction from a faithful exact finite-dimensional fibre functor
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $\mathcal A$ be an essentially small $k$-linear abelian category [def-sp-abelian]: its isomorphism classes form a set, its morphism sets are $k$-vector spaces and composition is bilinear. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\operatorname{Vect}^{\mathrm{fd}}_k$ be faithful, exact and $k$-linear, where finite-dimensional means having a finite spanning set [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Choose a small skeleton. Form the $k$-vector space
$$B=\left(\bigoplus_{V}F(V)^*\otimes_k F(V)\right)/N,$$
where $F(V)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_k(F(V),k)$, tensor products have their universal bilinear meaning [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and $N$ is the linear span of
$$[\psi\otimes F(f)v]_W-[\psi\circ F(f)\otimes v]_V\quad(f:V\to W,\ v\in F(V),\ \psi\in F(W)^*).$$
Brackets below denote classes in $B$; for nonskeletal objects use their chosen skeletal representatives. There is a counital coassociative coalgebra structure on $B$ with
$$\Delta[\phi\otimes v]_V=\sum_i[\phi\otimes e_i]_V\otimes[e_i^*\otimes v]_V,\qquad \epsilon[\phi\otimes v]_V=\phi(v),$$
independently of the choice of a finite basis $(e_i)$ of $F(V)$ with dual basis $(e_i^*)$. The formulas
$$\rho_V(v)=\sum_i e_i\otimes[e_i^*\otimes v]_V$$
define an equivalence from $\mathcal A$ to the category of finite-dimensional right $B$-comodules, sending $V$ to $(F(V),\rho_V)$ and $f$ to $F(f)$, whose composite with the underlying-vector-space functor is $F$. Here a right comodule is a vector space $M$ with a linear map $\rho:M\to M\otimes_kB$ satisfying $(\rho\otimes1)\rho=(1\otimes\Delta)\rho$ and $(1\otimes\epsilon)\rho=1_M$; its morphisms are linear maps commuting with $\rho$. No monoidal structure, dual objects, unit object or tensor compatibility of $F$ is assumed. All sums are set-indexed in a fixed containing universe.

source.place: Theorems 9.32 and 9.37, printed pp.175-178, and 9.41-9.43, pp.179-181. Explicit coefficient-quotient presentation of C(omega); an agent formulation of the coalgebra in Theorem 9.37, not a statement of neutral tensor reconstruction.

proof.text: Work on the chosen small skeleton, transporting finite sums, kernels and cokernels along the representative isomorphisms. For each object $X$, let $\mathcal C_X$ be the full subcategory of objects isomorphic to subquotients of finite sums of $X$. It is abelian [def-sp-abelian]: a kernel is a subobject of its source and a cokernel a quotient of its target; finite sums of subquotient presentations are again such presentations. An iterated subquotient is a subquotient, by taking the inverse image of the later subobject under the earlier quotient. Restrict $F$ to $\mathcal C_X$. Faithfulness and exactness show that $F$ detects zero objects and isomorphisms: a zero fibre gives $F(1_Y)=F(0)$ and hence $1_Y=0$; vanishing kernel and cokernel detect an isomorphism. Also $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,Z)$ embeds into $\operatorname{Hom}_k(FY,FZ)$, so all Hom spaces are finite-dimensional. These observations require no closure under extensions in the ambient category.

source.place: §9(d), p.175: initial observations and the category generated by X.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-single-generator-fibre-representability] to $F|\mathcal C_X$, obtaining $P,p$ and $\alpha_Y(h)=F(h)p$. Since $\alpha$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ with the exact faithful functor $F$, it is exact and detects zero morphisms. If $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ span $F(Y)$, let $h_i:P\to Y$ correspond to $v_i$. The morphism $(h_i):P^{\oplus n}\to Y$ has surjective fibre, so its cokernel has zero fibre and is zero. Thus it is an epimorphism, including $n=0$. All hypotheses of the projective-generator module lemma are now verified in $\mathcal C_X$.

source.place: Lemmas 9.33–9.34, p.176, followed by the finite-generator consequence.

proof.text: Put $R_X=\operatorname{End}(P)$, with multiplication composition, and $E_X=\operatorname{End}(F|\mathcal C_X)$, with pointwise composition. Under $\alpha$, the element $r\in R_X$ acts on $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Y)$ by $h\mapsto h\circ r$. These natural operators identify $E_X$ with $R_X^{\mathrm{op}}$: for a natural operator $t$, its value at $Y$ on $h$ is $h\circ r$, where $r$ is the element of $\operatorname{Hom}(P,P)$ corresponding to $t_P(p)$; this follows by naturality for $h:P\to Y$. Conversely this formula defines a natural operator, and composing two such operators reverses the order of $r$. In particular $E_X\to F(P)$, $t\mapsto t_Pp$, is a linear isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-projective-generator-module-equivalence]: $Y\mapsto F(Y)$, with its evaluation left $E_X$-action $t\cdot v=t_Yv$, is an equivalence onto finite-dimensional left $E_X$-modules. The algebra $E_X$ is finite-dimensional.

source.place: Lemma 9.35 and its concluding identification of natural endomorphisms, p.177; 9.41, p.180.

proof.text:
Write $c_V(\phi,v)$ for the class of $\phi\otimes v$ in the quotient $B$. A finite spanning family gives a finite basis by deleting dependent vectors (also use [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-free]); its identity tensor $\sum_i e_i\otimes e_i^*$ represents $1_{F(V)}$, so is basis independent. The finite tensor-dual isomorphism [lem-sfb-finite-free-tensor-dual] makes equality testable by pairs of linear functionals. Consequently the proposed $\Delta$ and $\epsilon$ are basis independent. They respect each relation for $T=F(f):F(V)\to F(W)$: if $e_i,b_a$ are bases, its two comultiplications are
$$\sum_a c_W(\psi,b_a)\otimes c_W(b_a^*,Tv)
=\sum_i c_W(\psi,Te_i)\otimes c_V(e_i^*,v)
=\sum_i c_V(\psi T,e_i)\otimes c_V(e_i^*,v).$$
The first equality expands $T$ in the two bases and uses the relation in the second tensor factor; the second uses it in the first factor. The counits on both sides are $\psi(Tv)$. Thus the linear formulas descend from the direct sum to $B$. Both iterated comultiplications give $\sum_{i,j}c_V(\phi,e_i)\otimes c_V(e_i^*,e_j)\otimes c_V(e_j^*,v)$ after renaming indices. Applying either counit reduces the sum to $c_V(\phi,v)$. This proves all coalgebra axioms. The same construction works for the quotient $B_X$ using just the objects and arrows of $\mathcal C_X$.

source.place: §9(d), pp.174–175: coefficient identities; agent calculation for the specified quotient presentation.

proof.text: The identical identity-tensor argument makes $\rho_V(v)=\sum_i e_i\otimes c_V(e_i^*,v)$ basis independent. Its counit is $v=\sum_i e_ie_i^*(v)$, and its two iterated coactions agree by the formula for $\Delta$. For $T=F(f)$, expand in bases $e_i,b_a$ and use $c_W(b_a^*,Tv)=c_V(b_a^*T,v)$ to obtain $\rho_WT=(T\otimes1)\rho_V$. Hence these formulas define the required functor $K$; the analogous functor $K_X$ has coefficients in $B_X$. All maps on underlying spaces are literally $F(f)$.

source.place: §9(d), pp.174–175; agent verification of naturality for the quotient.

proof.text:
The coalgebra $E_X^*$ and its module dictionary are supplied by [lem-sfb-finite-algebra-comodule-duality]. Define
$$\beta_X:B_X\longrightarrow E_X^*,\qquad \beta_X(c_V(\phi,v))(t)=\phi(t_Vv).$$
Naturality of $t$ makes this well defined. It is an isomorphism, as follows explicitly from the representing pair [lem-sfb-single-generator-fibre-representability]. For $v\in F(V)$ take the unique $h_v:P\to V$ with $F(h_v)p=v$. The defining relation gives $c_V(\phi,v)=c_P(\phi F(h_v),p)$, so $\psi\mapsto c_P(\psi,p)$ is surjective. Its composite with $\beta_X$ is the dual of the isomorphism $\eta_X:E_X\to F(P)$, $t\mapsto t_Pp$, computed in Step 3; its inverse sends $\mu\in E_X^*$ to $c_P(\mu\eta_X^{-1},p)$. This proves bijectivity without assuming the original quotient is finite-dimensional. For $t,s\in E_X$,
$$\langle(\beta_X\otimes\beta_X)\Delta c_V(\phi,v),t\otimes s\rangle=\sum_i\phi(t_Ve_i)e_i^*(s_Vv)=\phi(t_Vs_Vv).$$
The counit is evaluation at $1_{E_X}$. Thus $\beta_X$ is a coalgebra isomorphism, and $K_X(V)$ corresponds to the evaluation left action $t_V$ under the stated dictionary.

source.place: Theorem 9.37 and 9.41–9.42, pp.178–180; agent coefficient-quotient identification.

proof.text: By Steps 3 and 6 and [lem-sfb-finite-algebra-comodule-duality], $K_X:\mathcal C_X\to\operatorname{Comod}^{\mathrm{fd}}(B_X)$ is an equivalence. Namely Step 3 is an equivalence with left $E_X$-modules, the cited dictionary changes precisely those actions into right $E_X^*$-coactions, and $\beta_X^{-1}$ changes the coefficients to $B_X$. The calculation at the end of Step 6 identifies this composite with the displayed formula for $K_X$, on both objects and maps.

source.place: Lemma 9.35 and the paragraph after it, pp.177–178; Example 9.36.

proof.text: Index by the set of skeletal objects with preorder $X\preceq Y$ if $\mathcal C_X\subseteq\mathcal C_Y$; this need not be antisymmetric. It is nonempty (use $0$) and directed (use $X\oplus Y$). Inclusions induce coalgebra maps $B_X\to B_Y$ by sending each coefficient to the same coefficient. The cocone $B_X\to B$ is a vector-space colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: every generator occurs in $\mathcal C_V$, and every relation for $f:V\to W$ occurs in $\mathcal C_{V\oplus W}$. Thus any compatible family of linear maps out of the $B_X$ defines on generators a unique linear map out of $B$, and respects every defining relation. The coalgebra maps are compatible because their formulas on each generator coincide. No claim that transition maps are injective is used.

source.place: Theorem 9.37, p.178: directed system; agent verification of the quotient colimit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-directed-coalgebra-comodule-descent] to this small nonempty directed system. Its colimit coalgebra is the coalgebra already constructed on $B$, since the structure maps agree on every coefficient. Suppose $u:F(V)\to F(W)$ is a morphism of right $B$-comodules. Choose $X=V\oplus W$, so both coactions come from $B_X$. The eventual-colinearity clause gives $Y\succeq X$ for which $u$ is $B_Y$-colinear. The equivalence $K_Y$ of Step 7 gives $f:V\to W$ in the full subcategory $\mathcal C_Y$, with $F(f)=u$. Uniqueness follows from faithfulness of $F$. Therefore $K$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Theorem 9.37, p.178: passage to the directed limit, morphisms; finite module and comodule identifications above.

proof.text: Let $(M,\rho)$ be a finite-dimensional right $B$-comodule. The object-descent clause of [lem-sfb-directed-coalgebra-comodule-descent] gives a $B_X$-coaction on the same $M$ whose extension is $\rho$. By the equivalence $K_X$ of Step 7 this is isomorphic to $K_X(V)$ for some $V\in\mathcal C_X$. Extending the coaction gives an isomorphism $K(V)\simeq(M,\rho)$. Thus $K$ is essentially surjective and fully faithful, hence an equivalence. Its composite with the underlying-space functor is $F$ by construction. For a nonskeletal object and a chosen representative isomorphism $a$, the relation for $a$ identifies the coefficients and the equality $\rho F(a)=(F(a)\otimes1)\rho$ identifies the coactions. This gives the stipulated transport to the original category. If the category is zero, all coefficient spaces and $B$ are zero; the counit identity forces every right $0$-comodule to be zero, so this case is included.

source.place: Theorem 9.37, p.178: passage to the directed limit, objects and equivalence.

proof_origin.place: Milne §9(d), Theorem 9.37 via Lemmas 9.33–9.35, pp.175–178; the coefficient quotient, its local dual identification, and directed-limit details are written explicitly here.
